land.text: the Ottoman Hejaz, taken town by town in the Arab Revolt: Jeddah (16 June 1916), Mecca (9 July), Ta'if (22 September), Rabigh, Yanbu and al Qunfudhah (by the end of September 1916), Wejh (January 1917), Aqaba (6 July 1917)

predecessors.note: The Kingdom page lists 'Ottoman Hejaz' as the preceding state. Medina stayed Ottoman until the garrison surrendered 'on 9 January 1919'.

land.text: Jeddah, Yanbu, Medina and the rest of the kingdom's last shape, conquered by Nejd in December 1925 (Medina surrendered 9 December; infobox 'Conquered by Nejd on 19 December 1925')

successors.note: Cliopatria's Emirate of Nejd row ends in 1925; Ibn Saud was proclaimed King of Hejaz and the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd followed (infobox gives 8 January 1926 for the merger).

land.text: the same land as a dual monarchy of Hejaz and Nejd from 1926 (Cliopatria row 1926-1935)

successors.note: The Kingdom page's infobox lists 'Hejaz and Nejd' as the successor; 'Sharifian Caliphate' is also listed and is Hussein's claim of 5 March 1924, not a territorial state.

land.text: Ma'an and Aqaba, 'formally announced as annexed by Abdullah's Transjordan' after the Saudi conquest of the Hejaz (1924-1925)

successors.note: The Emirate of Transjordan (11 April 1921, Abdullah) became the Kingdom of Jordan; Cliopatria has no row before 1947, so the kingdom-of-jordan dossier should start in 1921.

capitals.name: Mecca
capitals.note: Infobox: Mecca (1916-1924). Mecca fell to Nejd on 13 October 1924 (Saudi conquest page).

capitals.name: Jeddah
capitals.note: Infobox: Jeddah (1924-1925). Jeddah was 'handed' to Ibn Saud in December 1925; the Saudis entered it on 8 January 1926.

rulers.name: Hussein bin Ali
rulers.title: King of the Hejaz
rulers.note: Infobox: 10 June 1916 to 3 October 1924 (abdicated). The Saudi conquest page has him 'abdicated as King of the Hejaz and fled' on 16 October 1924. He declared himself 'King of the Arab Countries' soon after the revolt began but the Allies 'recognized him only as King of the Hejaz' (Arab Revolt page).

rulers.name: Ali bin Hussein
rulers.title: King of the Hejaz
rulers.note: Infobox: 3 October 1924 to 19 December 1925 (deposed); the same infobox also lists 'Abdallah Siraj' for 1924-1925, unexplained.

correction.text: the towns the Sharifian army took in 1916: Mecca, Jeddah, Ta'if, Rabigh, Yanbu and al Qunfudhah, each a radius around the town (the page gives towns, not a frontier)

keyframe_review.note: 74.0 k km2 in Cliopatria, but the shape contains Yanbu only and none of Mecca, Jeddah, Ta'if or Rabigh. The Arab Revolt page has the revolt launched at Mecca on 10 June 1916, Jeddah surrendering 16 June, Mecca taken 9 July, Ta'if 22 September and 'Rabigh, Yanbu and al Qunfudhah' by the end of September 1916, so the 1916 state is the Mecca-Jeddah-Ta'if-Rabigh-Yanbu-Qunfudhah belt. Medina was never taken (garrison surrendered 9 January 1919). The Kingdom page gives no area (see the 1917 note).

correction.text: the Hejaz with Wejh and Aqaba, without Medina (Ottoman garrison to 9 January 1919) and without the Jordan plateau still Ottoman until Tafilah (January 1918) and Ma'an (September 1918)

keyframe_review.note: 339 k km2 (1,341 cells): the shape reaches 31.2 N and holds the Ma'an and Tafilah plateau and part of the Medina circle. Pages: Wejh fell 23 January 1917 and Aqaba 6 July 1917, but Tafilah only in January 1918 and Ma'an held out until late September 1918; Medina's garrison stayed Ottoman until 9 January 1919. Corrected: the shape without Medina and without Jordan beyond Aqaba, plus al Qunfudhah. Neither the Kingdom page nor the Arab Revolt page gives an area; the corrected 301 k km2 compares with the gazetteer's Hejaz region of 356 k km2 (ratio 0.85).

correction.text: the Hejaz proper with Aqaba and Ma'an 'and its hinterland (including Aqaba)'; Medina still Ottoman; Damascus and the north belong to Faisal's OETA East, not to the kingdom

keyframe_review.note: 433 k km2: Cliopatria carries the Hejaz north to Damascus (87 Syrian and about 256 Jordanian cells). The Arab Kingdom of Syria page lists the Kingdom of Hejaz separately from Faisal's Damascus government and does not say Syria was part of the Hejaz; the Arab Revolt page says Hussein's self-declared Hejaz state was the only part under his direct control at the end. The Transjordan page: Hussein annexed 'Ma'an and its hinterland (including Aqaba) to the Hejaz' in 1918 while OETA East and Faisal held Ma'an and Hussein never accepted this. Corrected: the Hejaz without Medina, Syria, Israel or northern Jordan, with Aqaba and Ma'an governorates kept.

correction.text: the Hejaz including Medina from 9 January 1919, with Aqaba and Ma'an; Syria and northern Transjordan are Faisal's administration, which is the arab-kingdom-of-syria dossier of this batch

keyframe_review.note: 434 k km2: as 1918 the shape includes Faisal's Syria and Transjordan. The Arab Kingdom of Syria page has Faisal's government announced 5 October 1918, the Damascus Program of 2 July 1919 and the kingdom proclaimed 8 March 1920, as a state of its own. Medina is rightly inside from 9 January 1919 (Arab Revolt page). Corrected: without Syria, Israel and northern Jordan; Aqaba and Ma'an governorates kept; Khurma was lost to the Saudis in 1918-1919 but lies outside the shape.

correction.text: the Hejaz with Aqaba and Ma'an, de facto under Hejaz control after Faisal's administration was defeated by the French

keyframe_review.note: 292.8 k km2: Cliopatria drops everything north of 30 N in 1920 (the Syrian-Jordanian lands went with Faisal's fall, 24-25 July 1920) but also drops Aqaba and Ma'an. The Transjordan page says Ma'an was de facto under Hejaz control after Faisal's administration was defeated by the French, and that Britain in August 1924 'cannot acquiesce in his claim' to administer Transjordan territory, read as a rejection of Hussein's claim to Ma'an, so Aqaba and Ma'an stay Hejazi until 1925. Corrected: the Cliopatria shape plus the Aqaba and Ma'an governorates. Abdullah marched into Ma'an on 21 November 1920 but with Hejazi backing, and the page does not say the Hejaz lost it then. The Kingdom was 'recognized 10 August 1920' (infobox).

correction.text: the Hejaz with Aqaba and Ma'an until their annexation by Transjordan in 1925

keyframe_review.note: 270.6 k km2: as 1920 without Aqaba and Ma'an, and with some northern Tabuk cells also gone (58 cells of Tabuk province outside the shape against 16 in 1920); no page opened explains the northern trim (the Wadi Sirhan proposal of 5 January 1922 is Lawrence's, not a border). Corrected by adding the Aqaba and Ma'an governorates as for 1920.

correction.text: the kingdom's last shape, Jeddah, Yanbu, Medina and the north, with Aqaba and Ma'an until 1925; Ta'if and Mecca are already outside this shape, which is the state after 13 October 1924, and the ledger dates their fall within 1924

keyframe_review.note: 214.6 k km2: the shape has already lost Ta'if and Mecca, which agrees with the Saudi conquest page (Ta'if surrendered after the advance of 29 August 1924, Mecca entered 13 October 1924, the Hashemites held only Jeddah, Yanbu and Medina), and it keeps Medina, Jeddah and Yanbu to the end of 1925 (Medina surrendered 9 December, Yanbu 12 days later, Jeddah handed over in December 1925). It also keeps Wejh, Rabigh and Tabuk, which the page does not mention. It lacks Aqaba and Ma'an, which Hussein's army held until they were 'formally announced as annexed by Abdullah's Transjordan'. For January-August 1924 the full 1923 kingdom stands; the ledger carries Ta'if and Mecca within 1924. Corrected: add Aqaba and Ma'an for 1924 (removed by the 1925 loss event).

region.text: Mecca, where the revolt was launched on 10 June 1916, and Jeddah, attacked the same day

ledger.note: 1916: Sharif Hussein launches the Arab Revolt at Mecca and the Kingdom of Hejaz begins. Infobox 'Established: Mecca Revolt, 10 June 1916'; the page says the state was 'self-proclaimed as a kingdom in June 1916'. Mecca itself fell on 9 July; Britain, France and Russia handed Hussein a note recognizing him as 'King of the Hedjaz' on 10 December 1916 (Kingdom page) and the infobox adds 'Recognized 10 August 1920'. The page names towns, not a frontier.

region.text: the Ottoman garrison of Medina under Fakhri Pasha

ledger.note: 1916: the Hashemites besiege Ottoman Medina. 'On 5 June 1916 Emirs Ali and Faisal attacked the Ottoman garrison in Medina but were defeated' by 'an aggressive Turkish defence, led by Fakhri Pasha'; the town stayed Ottoman to 9 January 1919.
1916: Jeddah falls to the Revolt. The Ottoman garrison surrendered at Jeddah on 16 June 1916 after an attack on 10 June by about 3,500 Arabs with British warship bombardment.
1916: Mecca is taken. Mecca was taken on 9 July 1916, with Egyptian troops providing artillery support.
1916: Ta'if is taken. Ta'if was taken by Abdullah on 22 September 1916, with Egyptian artillery support.
1916: the Red Sea ports fall. By the end of September 1916 the Sharifian Army had taken Rabigh, Yanbu and al Qunfudhah 'with the assistance of the Royal Navy'.
1917: Wejh is taken. It was attacked from the north on 23 January 1917 and 'surrendered within 36 hours'.
1917: Aqaba falls. 'On 6 July, after an overland attack, Aqaba fell to those Arab forces with only a handful of casualties.' The Transjordan page adds that Ottoman forces withdrew from Aqaba in 1917.

region.text: Ma'an and its hinterland, including Aqaba

ledger.note: 1918: Ma'an and its hinterland pass to the Hejazi claim. Hussein annexed 'Ma'an and its hinterland (including Aqaba) to the Hejaz' after the Ottoman collapse (footnote of the Transjordan page); the Arab Revolt page has the Ottoman garrison of Ma'an cut off by the Sharifian Army and holding out until late September 1918. The Transjordan page also says OETA East and Faisal's Syria held Ma'an and Hussein never accepted that, so the holding is de jure rather than administered until 1920.

region.text: al-Khurma, on the Hejaz-Nejd frontier (an approximate position; the page gives no coordinates)

ledger.note: 1918: the Hejaz and the Saudis fight over al-Khurma. The Unification of Saudi Arabia page: the Saudis and their Ikhwan allies fought the Hashemites of Hejaz in the al-Khurma dispute of 1918-1919. The page gives the span, not a month.

1919: al-Khurma is lost. 'It resulted in the defeat of the Hashemite forces and capture of al-Khurma by the Saudis'; British intervention produced a ceasefire that lasted until 1924. Cliopatria's Hejaz shapes never include Khurma (0 of 3 cells at the town), so no shape changes.
1919: the al-Khurma fighting ends in a British-brokered ceasefire that lasted until 1924.
1919: Medina's garrison surrenders. Fakhri Pasha gave up Medina only 'when ordered to by the Turkish government on 9 January 1919' (456 officers and 9,364 soldiers).
1919: Medina passes to the Hejaz. The Ottoman garrison surrendered on 9 January 1919, so the Hejaz holds Medina from this date.

region.text: Ta'if and Mecca, the part of the kingdom lost to the first Saudi advance

ledger.note: 1924: the Saudi campaign against the Hejaz opens. Ibn Saud declared jihad on Hussein in August 1924, and on 29 August 1924 advanced toward Taif, which 'surrendered without a major struggle'. The pretext was that pilgrims from Nejd were denied access to the holy places; the caliphate claim of Hussein (5 March 1924) and the end of British subsidies (late 1923) preceded it.

1924: Ta'if surrenders to the Saudis. The page has the advance of 29 August 1924 on Ta'if, which 'surrendered without a major struggle'; it gives no day for the surrender. Month 9 (reviewer me-10-g): the page puts Ta'if's surrender after the campaign's start on 29 August and before Mecca's fall on 13 October 1924.
1924: Mecca falls. 'The city of Mecca fell without struggle' on 13 October 1924; Hussein 'abdicated as King of the Hejaz and fled' (16 October on this page, 3 October in the Kingdom page's infobox).
1924: the first contest ends with Ta'if and Mecca in Saudi hands. By the end of October 1924 the Hashemites held only Jeddah, Yanbu and Medina.

region.text: Jeddah, Yanbu, Medina and the north, the kingdom's last shape

ledger.note: 1924: the siege of the remnant begins. By the end of October 1924 the Hashemites held only Jeddah, Yanbu and Medina and a blockade of Jeddah followed.
1924: the capital moves to Jeddah. Infobox: 'Mecca (1916-1924), then Jeddah (1924-1925)', after Mecca fell on 13 October 1924.

1925: Aqaba and Ma'an pass to Transjordan. After the Saudi conquest of the Hejaz Hussein's army 'fled to the Ma'an region, which was then formally announced as annexed by Abdullah's Transjordan'. The page gives the span 1924-1925, so the year is the page's and the month is not known; in August 1924 Britain had already told Hussein it 'cannot acquiesce in his claim' to administer Transjordan territory (cable to Bullard).
1925: Medina surrenders to the Saudis. 'Medina surrendered on 9 December' (one source; the University of Indiana source gives 5 December).
1925: Yanbu falls. It 'fell 12 days later' than Medina, so about 21 December 1925 on the page's own count.

region.text: Jeddah, Yanbu, Medina and the north

ledger.note: 1925: the last contest ends with the fall of Jeddah. The campaign 'successfully ended in December 1925, with the fall of Jeddah' (Unification of Saudi Arabia page); the Saudi conquest page has Jeddah handed to Ibn Saud in December 1925 and the Saudi forces entering on 8 January 1926.

region.text: the kingdom's last shape: Jeddah, Yanbu, Medina and the north; Ma'an and Aqaba had passed to Transjordan

ledger.note: 1925: the Kingdom of Hejaz ends. Infobox: 'Conquered by Nejd on 19 December 1925'; Ali bin Hussein was deposed. The Arab Revolt page has 'on 23 December 1925 King Hussein bin Ali surrendered to the Saudis'; the infobox adds 8 January 1926 for the merger into the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd.

wars.name: Arab Revolt

zones.text: Medina, besieged but never taken until the garrison's surrender on 9 January 1919
Ma'an, whose garrison held out to late September 1918

wars.outcome: The Ottomans lost the Hejaz town by town (Jeddah 16 June, Mecca 9 July, Ta'if 22 September 1916, Wejh January 1917, Aqaba July 1917, Ma'an September 1918) and Medina surrendered on 9 January 1919; Hussein, self-declared 'King of the Arab Countries', was recognized only as King of the Hejaz.
wars.note: The Egyptian Expeditionary Force, not Hussein, seized Palestine, Transjordan, Lebanon and southern Syria; Faisal's Arab army entered Damascus on 1 October 1918 and his government there is not part of the Kingdom.

wars.name: Al-Khurma dispute
wars.outcome: The Hashemite forces were defeated and al-Khurma was captured by the Saudis; British intervention produced a ceasefire that lasted until 1924.
wars.note: The Unification page does not name the battle of Turaba; the Wikipedia pages 'Battle of Turaba' and 'Battle of Turabah' returned url_not_found, so the Turaba cells that Cliopatria keeps in the Hejaz to 1923 are unverified.

wars.name: Saudi conquest of Hejaz

zones.text: the whole kingdom: Ta'if and Mecca first, then the blockaded remnant of Jeddah, Yanbu and Medina

wars.outcome: Nejd took Ta'if (August-September 1924), Mecca (13 October 1924), Medina (9 December 1925), Yanbu (about 21 December) and Jeddah (December 1925); Hussein abdicated in October 1924 and Ali was deposed on 19 December 1925; Transjordan annexed Ma'an and Aqaba.
wars.note: Transjordan's King Abdullah asked for help and was denied. Ibn Saud was proclaimed King of Hejaz and the dual Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd followed in 1926.

certainty.note: Every frontier is a desert or tribal one; no page opened gives a treaty line. The Ma'an-Aqaba frontier with Transjordan is disputed and soft throughout; the coastal towns taken in 1916-1917 are points, drawn as circles.

sources.title: Kingdom of Hejaz
sources.note: Infobox (established 10 June 1916, dissolved 19 December 1925, capitals, rulers, recognition 10 August 1920, population); no area figure on the page.

sources.title: Arab Revolt
sources.note: Dated captures of Jeddah, Mecca, Ta'if, the Red Sea ports, Wejh, Aqaba, Tafilah, Ma'an, Deraa, Damascus; Medina's surrender 9 January 1919; Hussein's title.

sources.title: Saudi conquest of Hejaz
sources.note: The 1924-1925 campaign: Ta'if, Mecca, Medina, Yanbu, Jeddah, Hussein's abdication, Ali bin Hussein.

sources.title: Emirate of Transjordan
sources.note: Aqaba and Ma'an: annexed by Hussein in 1918, de facto Hejazi after July 1920, annexed by Transjordan 1925; Abdullah at Ma'an 21 November 1920.

sources.title: Arab Kingdom of Syria
sources.note: Faisal's OETA East and kingdom as a state apart from the Hejaz (5 October 1918, 8 March 1920, 24-25 July 1920); the Damascus Program's southern limit.

sources.title: Unification of Saudi Arabia
sources.note: Shared with asir and north-yemen: the al-Khurma dispute of 1918-1919, the end of the Hejaz campaign in December 1925, the proclamation of 1926.

notes: Pages opened: Kingdom of Hejaz, Arab Revolt, Saudi conquest of Hejaz, Emirate of Transjordan, Arab Kingdom of Syria, plus Unification of Saudi Arabia (shared with asir and north-yemen; counted against their budgets). 'Battle of Turaba' and 'Battle of Turabah' returned url_not_found. Cliopatria rows to correct: the 1916 shape holds Yanbu only and none of Mecca, Jeddah or Ta'if; the 1917-1919 shapes carry Faisal's Syria and Transjordan (up to Damascus) and, to 1918, the Ottoman-held Ma'an plateau and a part of Medina, none of which the pages give the Hejaz; 1920-1923 drop Aqaba and Ma'an, which were Hejazi de facto until 1925; the Turaba cells stay inside to 1923 with no page. No area figure on the Kingdom page, so the infobox comparison could not be made; the corrected 1917 shape (301 k km2) is 0.85 of the gazetteer's Hejaz region (356 k km2). Counterparts: arab-kingdom-of-syria (Faisal's OETA East 1918-1920, kingdom 8 March - 25 July 1920) is written in this batch (me-10-g) because no Cliopatria row covers it; the Emirate of Transjordan (1921-1946) is the early life of kingdom-of-jordan, whose dossier should start in 1921; the Cliopatria Emirate of Nejd row (slug emirate-of-nejd, group me-10) is the Saudi side of every loss. Disagreements: Hussein's end of reign 3 October 1924 (Kingdom infobox) against 16 October 1924 (Saudi conquest page); the kingdom's end 19 December 1925 (infobox), 23 December 1925 (Arab Revolt page, Kingdom text) and 8 January 1926 (Jeddah entered); Medina's surrender 9 December against 5 December 1925; the Kingdom infobox also lists Ali for 1916-1924 and 'Abdallah Siraj' for 1924-1925. The Kingdom page gives 'self-proclaimed as a kingdom in June 1916' with no October or November proclamation date. Not settled: the exact Hejaz-Asir frontier at al Qunfudhah, the Hejaz-Nejd frontier between 1919 and 1924, the northern Tabuk trim of 1922, whether Ma'an was administered by the Hejaz or by OETA East in 1918-1920. Gazetteer names needed: Rabigh (a 50 km radius at 39.03 E 22.8 N is used), Al Khurmah (a 50 km radius at 42.0 E 21.9 N is used, approximate). The Hejaz kingdom's Wejh, Tabuk and Rabigh holdings in the Saudi-conquest shape are the Cliopatria shape's, not the page's.
